title: Two-digit numbers with digit sum 5
statement:
Swathi lists every two-digit number whose two digits add up to 5.
How many numbers are on her list?
keySteps: The tens digit cannot be 0, so it can be 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5.
For each tens digit the units digit is fixed as 5 minus it.
The numbers are 14, 23, 32, 41 and 50, which is 5 numbers.
explanation: The tens digit t must be from 1 to 5 (it cannot be 0), and the units digit is then 5 − t, which is always between 0 and 4. That gives 14, 23, 32, 41 and 50. Check: each pair of digits adds to 5, and 05 is not a two-digit number, so the count is 5.
hints: Start with the tens digit and ask what the units digit must be.
The tens digit of a two-digit number cannot be 0.
Write them out: 14, 23, ... and count.

title: Digits used to number 50 pages
statement:
Rahul numbers the pages of his lab record from 1 to 50.
How many digits does he write in total?
keySteps: Pages 1 to 9 are single-digit: 9 digits.
Pages 10 to 50 are 41 two-digit numbers: 41 × 2 = 82 digits.
explanation: Pages 1–9 use one digit each, which is 9 digits. Pages 10–50 are 50 − 10 + 1 = 41 pages with two digits each, which is 82 digits. Total 9 + 82 = 91. Check: 50 pages would be 100 digits if all were two-digit; the 9 single-digit pages save 9, giving 91.
hints: Split the pages into one-digit and two-digit page numbers.
How many numbers are there from 10 to 50? Remember to count both ends.
9 one-digit pages and 41 two-digit pages.

title: Largest three-digit multiple of 7
statement: What is the largest three-digit number that is exactly divisible by 7?
keySteps: The largest three-digit number is 999.
Divide 999 by 7: 7 × 142 = 994 with remainder 5.
Subtract the remainder: 999 − 5 = 994.
explanation: 999 ÷ 7 gives quotient 142 and remainder 5, because 7 × 142 = 994. Removing the remainder gives 994. Check: the next multiple, 994 + 7 = 1001, has four digits, so 994 is the largest.
hints: Start from 999, the largest three-digit number.
Find the remainder when 999 is divided by 7.

title: Sum of ages six years later
statement:
The present ages of Suresh and his father add up to 48 years.
What will the sum of their ages be 6 years from now?
keySteps: Each person gets 6 years older.
Two people together gain 2 × 6 = 12 years.
explanation: In 6 years Suresh gains 6 years and his father also gains 6 years, so the total rises by 12. The sum becomes 48 + 12 = 60. Check with any example: 12 and 36 now become 18 and 42, and 18 + 42 = 60.
hints: You do not need their individual ages.
How much older does each of the two people become?
Add 6 for each person to the total.

title: Brother's age when Meena turns 20
statement:
Meena is 8 years old and her brother Kartik is 14 years old.
How old will Kartik be when Meena is 20?
keySteps: The age difference is 14 − 8 = 6 years.
The difference between two people's ages never changes.
When Meena is 20, Kartik is 20 + 6 = 26.
explanation: Kartik is 6 years older than Meena and that difference stays the same forever. When Meena is 20, Kartik will be 26. Check: Meena needs 12 more years to reach 20, and 14 + 12 = 26.
hints: Find how much older Kartik is.
An age gap does not grow or shrink over time.
Add the gap to 20.

title: Ages in ratio 4 : 7
statement:
The ages of Anil and Sunil are in the ratio 4 : 7. Sunil is 9 years older than Anil.
How old is Anil?
keySteps: Let the ages be 4k and 7k.
The difference is 7k − 4k = 3k = 9, so k = 3.
explanation: Write the ages as 4k and 7k. Their difference 3k equals 9 years, so k = 3, making Anil 12 and Sunil 21. Check: 12 : 21 simplifies to 4 : 7 and 21 − 12 = 9.
hints: Write each age as a multiple of the same number k.
The difference of 3 parts is 9 years.
One part is 3 years; Anil has 4 parts.

title: Trees along a 100 m road
statement:
The municipality plants a tree every 10 metres along one side of a straight 100 m road, with a tree at both ends.
How many trees are planted?
keySteps: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 gaps between trees.
With trees at both ends, the number of trees is one more than the gaps.
explanation: The road is split into 100 ÷ 10 = 10 equal gaps. A row with a tree at each end always has one more tree than gaps, so there are 11 trees. Check with a short road: 20 m has 2 gaps and trees at 0, 10, 20 — that is 3 trees.
hints: Count the gaps first.
Draw a 20 m road with trees every 10 m and count.
Trees = gaps + 1 when both ends have a tree.

title: Metro card trips
statement:
Pooja's metro card has a balance of Rs 200. Each trip costs Rs 35.
How many complete trips can she take before she must recharge?
keySteps: Divide 200 by 35.
She can take 5 full trips, with Rs 25 left over.
explanation: 200 ÷ 35 gives quotient 5 and remainder 25, since 35 × 5 = 175. A sixth trip would need Rs 210, more than her balance. Check: 175 + 25 = 200.
hints: How many 35s fit into 200?
Try 35 × 5 and 35 × 6.
The leftover Rs 25 is not enough for another trip.

title: Splitting the biryani bill
statement:
Seven friends order biryani. The bill is Rs 1,260 and they add a Rs 140 tip. They split the total equally.
How much does each friend pay, in rupees?
keySteps: Total to pay = 1260 + 140 = 1400.
Divide by the number of friends: 1400 ÷ 7.
Each pays Rs 200.
explanation: The total including tip is Rs 1,400. Shared equally by 7 friends, that is 1400 ÷ 7 = Rs 200 each. Check: 7 × 200 = 1400.
hints: Add the tip to the bill first.
Then share the total among 7 people.

title: Angle at 4 o'clock
statement: What is the smaller angle, in degrees, between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at exactly 4:00?
keySteps: The 12 hour marks split 360° into 30° each.
At 4:00 the minute hand is on 12 and the hour hand is on 4.
They are 4 marks apart: 4 × 30 = 120°.
explanation: Each hour mark is 360 ÷ 12 = 30° apart. At 4:00 the hands point at 12 and 4, which are 4 marks apart, so the angle is 120°. Check: the other way round is 8 marks = 240°, and 120 + 240 = 360, so 120° is the smaller angle.
hints: How many degrees between two neighbouring numbers on a clock?
Where are the two hands at exactly 4:00?
4 gaps of 30° each.

title: From 10 February to 10 March
statement:
In 2027 (not a leap year), Arjun's project starts on 10 February and his review is on 10 March.
How many days after the start is the review?
keySteps: 2027 is not a leap year, so February has 28 days.
From 10 Feb to 28 Feb is 18 days.
From 28 Feb to 10 March is 10 more days: 18 + 10 = 28.
explanation: From 10 February to 28 February is 18 days, and from 28 February to 10 March is 10 more days, total 28. Check: a non-leap February has 28 days, and moving from the 10th of February to the 10th of March crosses exactly February's length.
hints: How many days does February have in a non-leap year?
Count from 10 Feb to the end of February, then into March.
18 days to 28 Feb plus 10 days.

title: Clock strikes from 1 to 6
statement:
A wall clock strikes once at 1 o'clock, twice at 2 o'clock, and so on (it strikes only on the hour).
How many strikes does it make from 1 pm to 6 pm, counting both 1 pm and 6 pm?
keySteps: The strikes are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6.
Total = 21.
explanation: At 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 pm the clock strikes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 times. Adding gives 21. Check with the formula n(n + 1)/2 = 6 × 7 / 2 = 21.
hints: List how many times it strikes at each hour.
Only the hours 1 to 6 pm count.

title: Overnight train journey
statement:
The Charminar Express leaves at 10:45 pm and reaches its destination at 6:20 am the next morning.
How many minutes long is the journey?
keySteps: From 10:45 pm to midnight is 1 hour 15 minutes.
From midnight to 6:20 am is 6 hours 20 minutes.
Total 7 hours 35 minutes = 7 × 60 + 35 = 455 minutes.
explanation: Split the trip at midnight: 1 h 15 min before and 6 h 20 min after, giving 7 h 35 min. In minutes that is 420 + 35 = 455. Check: 10:45 pm plus 7 h is 5:45 am, plus 35 min is 6:20 am.
hints: Break the journey at midnight.
Add the two parts in hours and minutes.
Convert 7 h 35 min to minutes.

title: Chocolates for wrappers
statement:
A shop sells chocolates at Rs 1 each and also gives 1 free chocolate for every 3 wrappers returned. Wrappers of free chocolates can be returned too, but the shop does not lend wrappers.
Kiran has Rs 15. What is the largest number of chocolates he can eat?
keySteps: Buy 15 chocolates and keep 15 wrappers.
15 wrappers give 5 chocolates, leaving 5 wrappers.
5 wrappers give 1 chocolate with 2 left; that makes 3 wrappers, which give 1 more.
1 wrapper is left over; total = 15 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 22.
explanation: He buys 15 and gets 15 wrappers. Exchanging 15 wrappers gives 5 more chocolates (5 wrappers). Exchanging 3 of those gives 1 chocolate, so he now holds 2 + 1 = 3 wrappers, which give 1 more. He ends with 1 wrapper, which cannot be exchanged. Total 15 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 22.
hints: Keep track of the wrappers after every exchange.
After the first exchange he has 5 chocolates and so 5 new wrappers.
Leftover wrappers combine with new ones — do not throw them away.

title: Counting the digit 7
statement:
Lakshmi writes all the whole numbers from 1 to 100.
How many times does she write the digit 7?
keySteps: Count 7 in the units place: 7, 17, 27, ..., 97 gives 10 times.
Count 7 in the tens place: 70 to 79 gives 10 times.
77 has a 7 in both places and is counted once in each list, which is correct because it has two 7s.
explanation: In the units place, 7 appears in 7, 17, ..., 97, which is 10 numbers. In the tens place, 7 appears in 70–79, another 10. The number 77 contains two 7s, so counting it once in each list is right. Total 20. Check: 100 contains no 7.
hints: Count the units place and the tens place separately.
How many numbers from 70 to 79?
77 has two 7s — make sure it contributes 2.

title: Number four times its digit sum
statement:
A two-digit number is equal to 4 times the sum of its digits. Its units digit is 3 more than its tens digit.
What is the number?
keySteps: Let the number be 10a + b, so 10a + b = 4(a + b).
Simplify: 6a = 3b, so b = 2a.
Use b = a + 3: 2a = a + 3, so a = 3 and b = 6.
The number is 36.
explanation: With tens digit a and units digit b, 10a + b = 4a + 4b gives 6a = 3b, so b = 2a. Since b = a + 3, we get a = 3 and b = 6, so the number is 36. Check: 3 + 6 = 9 and 4 × 9 = 36, and 6 is 3 more than 3.
hints: Write the number as 10a + b.
The first condition simplifies to b = 2a.
Combine b = 2a with b = a + 3.

title: Grandfather eight times as old
statement:
Ramaiah is 8 times as old as his grandson. In 6 years, the sum of their ages will be 84.
How old is Ramaiah now?
keySteps: In 6 years both gain 6, so the present sum is 84 − 12 = 72.
Let the grandson be x; Ramaiah is 8x, so 9x = 72.
x = 8, so Ramaiah = 64.
explanation: The future sum 84 includes 6 extra years for each of the two people, so today's sum is 72. With ages x and 8x, 9x = 72 gives x = 8 and Ramaiah = 64. Check: in 6 years they are 70 and 14, and 70 + 14 = 84.
hints: First find the sum of their present ages.
Subtract 6 years for each person from 84.
Grandson x, grandfather 8x, total 9x.

title: Baby joins the family
statement:
Three years ago, the average age of a family of 5 members was 17 years. A baby has been born since then, and today the average age of all 6 members is still 17 years.
How old is the baby?
keySteps: Three years ago the 5 members' total age was 5 × 17 = 85.
Today those 5 have total 85 + 5 × 3 = 100.
Today's total for 6 members is 6 × 17 = 102.
Baby's age = 102 − 100 = 2.
explanation: The 5 older members totalled 85 three years ago and have each gained 3 years, so they total 100 now. The 6 members together total 6 × 17 = 102, so the baby is 2 years old. Check: the baby is younger than 3, which fits being born within the last 3 years.
hints: Turn each average into a total.
Each of the 5 original members is 3 years older now.
Compare 6 × 17 with the 5 members' total today.

title: Negative marking test
statement:
An entrance test has 50 questions. Each correct answer gets +4 and each wrong answer gets −1. Ananya answered all 50 and scored 130.
How many did she get right?
keySteps: Let c be correct; wrong = 50 − c.
explanation: If c answers are correct, the other 50 − c are wrong, so 4c − (50 − c) = 130. This gives 5c = 180 and c = 36. Check: 36 × 4 = 144, 14 wrong cost 14, and 144 − 14 = 130.
hints: Use one letter for correct answers; wrong answers are the rest.
Each wrong answer subtracts 1.

title: Angle at 3:40
statement: What is the smaller angle, in degrees, between the hands of a clock at 3:40?
keySteps: The minute hand at 40 minutes is at 40 × 6 = 240°.
The hour hand moves 0.5° per minute: 3 × 30 + 40 × 0.5 = 110°.
Difference = 240 − 110 = 130°, which is less than 180°.
explanation: Measured from 12, the minute hand is at 240° and the hour hand is at 90° + 20° = 110°, because it has moved two-thirds of the way from 3 to 4. The difference is 130°. Check with the formula |30H − 5.5M| = |90 − 220| = 130.
hints: The hour hand is not exactly on 3 at 3:40.
Minute hand: 6° per minute. Hour hand: 0.5° per minute.
Find both positions measured from 12 and subtract.

title: Fast clock shows 6 pm
statement:
A clock gains 4 minutes every hour. It is set to the correct time at 6:00 am.
When this clock shows 6:00 pm the same day, what is the correct time?
keySteps: In 60 real minutes the clock moves 64 minutes.
From 6 am to 6 pm the clock has moved 12 hours = 720 minutes.
Real time passed = 720 × 60 / 64 = 675 minutes = 11 h 15 min.
Correct time = 6:00 am + 11 h 15 min = 5:15 pm.
explanation: The clock runs 64 minutes for every 60 real minutes. It has shown 720 minutes pass, so the real time passed is 720 × 60/64 = 675 minutes, which is 11 hours 15 minutes. The true time is 5:15 pm. Check: in 11.25 real hours the clock gains 11.25 × 4 = 45 minutes, and 5:15 pm + 45 min = 6:00 pm.
hints: The clock shows more time than really passed.
Compare 64 clock-minutes with 60 real minutes.
720 clock-minutes × 60/64 real minutes.

title: Pens and pencils
statement:
3 pens and 2 pencils cost Rs 46. 2 pens and 3 pencils cost Rs 39.
What is the cost of one pen, in rupees?
keySteps: Add the two: 5 pens + 5 pencils = 85, so 1 pen + 1 pencil = 17.
Subtract the second from the first: 1 pen − 1 pencil = 7.
Add the results: 2 pens = 24, so a pen costs 12.
explanation: Adding the two purchases gives 5 pens and 5 pencils for Rs 85, so one of each costs Rs 17. Subtracting them gives pen − pencil = Rs 7. So a pen is (17 + 7)/2 = Rs 12 and a pencil Rs 5. Check: 36 + 10 = 46 and 24 + 15 = 39.
hints: Try adding the two statements together.
Then try subtracting one from the other.
pen + pencil = 17 and pen − pencil = 7.

title: Right angles from noon to midnight
statement: Between 12 noon and 12 midnight, how many times are the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock exactly at a right angle (90°) to each other?
keySteps: The minute hand gains 330° on the hour hand every hour, so it laps the hour hand 11 times in 12 hours.
In each lap, the gap between the hands passes 90° and 270°, giving two right angles.
That gives 11 × 2 = 22 right angles in 12 hours.
It is not 2 per hour (24) because the right angles at 3:00 and 9:00 are each shared by two neighbouring hours.
explanation: In 12 hours the minute hand laps the hour hand 11 times (they meet only 11 times, not 12). In every lap the gap between them passes through 90° and 270°, so they form a right angle twice per lap: 11 × 2 = 22. Check: a naive count of 2 per hour gives 24, but the hours 2–3 and 3–4 share the single right angle at 3:00, and 8–9 and 9–10 share 9:00, so 24 − 2 = 22.
hints: Think about how often the minute hand catches up with the hour hand.
The hands meet 11 times in 12 hours, not 12.
Each meeting-to-meeting cycle has two right angles.

title: Unit digit of 3 to the 25
statement: What is the unit (last) digit of 3^25 (3 raised to the power 25)?
keySteps: Unit digits of powers of 3 repeat: 3, 9, 7, 1.
The cycle length is 4.
25 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 1, so the unit digit is the first in the cycle: 3.
explanation: The last digits of 3^1, 3^2, 3^3, 3^4 are 3, 9, 7, 1 and then repeat. Since 25 = 4 × 6 + 1, 3^25 has the same last digit as 3^1, which is 3. Check: 3^5 = 243 also ends in 3, matching the cycle.
hints: Write the last digits of 3, 9, 27, 81, 243.
The last digits repeat every 4 powers.
Find 25 mod 4.

title: Father's age when son is 18
statement:
Mohan was 26 years old when his son was born. His son is now 9.
How old will Mohan be when his son is 18?
keySteps: Mohan is always 26 years older than his son.
When the son is 18, Mohan is 18 + 26.
Mohan will be 44.
explanation: The age gap between father and son is fixed at 26 years. When the son is 18, Mohan is 18 + 26 = 44. Check: today Mohan is 35; in 9 years he is 44 and the son is 18.
hints: The son's current age is not really needed.
What is the fixed gap between their ages?
Add 26 to 18.

title: Notebooks and pens
statement:
The cost of 12 notebooks is the same as the cost of 15 pens. One pen costs Rs 20.
What is the cost of one notebook, in rupees?
keySteps: 15 pens cost 15 × 20 = Rs 300.
So 12 notebooks cost Rs 300.
One notebook costs 300 ÷ 12 = Rs 25.
explanation: 15 pens cost Rs 300, and that equals the price of 12 notebooks, so a notebook is 300 ÷ 12 = Rs 25. Check: 12 × 25 = 300 = 15 × 20.
hints: Find the cost of 15 pens first.
That same amount buys 12 notebooks.

title: Clock seen in a mirror
statement:
Divya sees a wall clock reflected in a mirror. The reflection appears to show 4:20.
What is the actual time?
keySteps: A mirror flips the clock left to right.
For a reflection, actual time = 11:60 − shown time.
explanation: In a mirror, the actual time and the reflected time always add up to 12:00. So the actual time is 12:00 − 4:20 = 7:40. Check: at 7:40 the minute hand is on 8 and the hour hand between 7 and 8; flipped, the minute hand appears on 4 and the hour hand between 4 and 5, which reads 4:20.
hints: The real time and the mirror time add up to 12:00.
Write 12:00 as 11:60 to subtract easily.

title: Trailing zeros of 50 factorial
statement: How many zeros are there at the end of 50! (50 factorial = 1 × 2 × 3 × ... × 50)?
keySteps: Each trailing zero comes from a factor 10 = 2 × 5; 5s are scarcer than 2s.
Multiples of 5 up to 50: 50 ÷ 5 = 10.
Multiples of 25 give an extra 5: 50 ÷ 25 = 2.
Total 5s = 10 + 2 = 12, so 12 zeros.
explanation: Trailing zeros are made by pairs of 2 and 5, and there are far more 2s than 5s, so count the 5s. There are 10 multiples of 5 up to 50, and 25 and 50 each contribute one extra 5, giving 12. Check: 125 > 50, so no further terms.
hints: A zero at the end needs a factor of 10.
Count how many factors of 5 appear in 1 × 2 × ... × 50.
Do not forget 25 and 50 contain 5 twice.

title: Remainder of 2 to the 100 by 7
statement: What is the remainder when 2^100 is divided by 7?
keySteps: 2^3 = 8 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 7.
(2^3)^33 leaves remainder 1, so 2^100 leaves remainder 1 × 2 = 2.
explanation: Since 8 leaves remainder 1 by 7, any power of 2^3 also leaves remainder 1. Writing 2^100 = (2^3)^33 × 2 gives remainder 2. Check the cycle: remainders of 2^1, 2^2, 2^3, 2^4 are 2, 4, 1, 2 — period 3, and 100 mod 3 = 1, so it matches 2^1.
hints: Find a small power of 2 that leaves remainder 1 by 7.
Split 100 into a multiple of 3 plus a remainder.

title: Product of two ages
statement:
Priya is 6 years older than her cousin Rahul. The product of their present ages is 216.
How old is Priya?
keySteps: Let Rahul be x; Priya is x + 6, so x(x + 6) = 216.
x² + 6x − 216 = 0 factors as (x + 18)(x − 12) = 0.
Age cannot be negative, so x = 12 and Priya = 18.
explanation: With Rahul x, x(x + 6) = 216, i.e. x² + 6x − 216 = 0 = (x − 12)(x + 18). The positive root is x = 12, so Priya is 18. Check: 12 × 18 = 216 and 18 − 12 = 6.
hints: Use one variable for Rahul's age.
Form a quadratic and factor it.
Look for two numbers 6 apart that multiply to 216.

title: Three ages adding to 27
statement:
Asha is 2 years older than Bhanu. Bhanu is twice as old as Chetan. The total of their three ages is 27.
How old is Bhanu?
keySteps: Let Chetan be x; Bhanu = 2x and Asha = 2x + 2.
Total: x + 2x + 2x + 2 = 27, so 5x = 25.
x = 5, so Bhanu = 10.
explanation: Expressing everyone in terms of Chetan's age x gives x + 2x + (2x + 2) = 27, so 5x = 25 and x = 5. Bhanu is 10 and Asha is 12. Check: 12 + 10 + 5 = 27, 12 is 2 more than 10, and 10 is twice 5.
hints: Pick the youngest person as x.
Write Bhanu and Asha in terms of x.

title: Hostel food stock
statement:
A hostel has food for 120 students for 30 days. After 10 days, 40 new students join.
For how many more days will the remaining food last?
keySteps: Total food = 120 × 30 = 3600 student-days.
After 10 days, 120 × 20 = 2400 student-days remain.
Now there are 160 students: 2400 ÷ 160 = 15 days.
explanation: Measure food in student-days. After 10 days the food left would have fed 120 students for 20 more days, i.e. 2400 student-days. Shared among 160 students, it lasts 2400 ÷ 160 = 15 days. Check: 160 × 15 = 2400.
hints: Measure the food in 'student-days'.
How much is left after the first 10 days?
Divide what is left by the new number of students.

title: Coins in a temple box
statement:
A temple donation box has only Re 1, 50 paise and 25 paise coins, in the ratio 5 : 6 : 8 by number. The total value is Rs 210.
How many 50 paise coins are there?
keySteps: Let the coins be 5k, 6k and 8k.
Value in rupees: 5k × 1 + 6k × 0.5 + 8k × 0.25 = 5k + 3k + 2k = 10k.
50 paise coins = 6 × 21 = 126.
explanation: With 5k, 6k and 8k coins, the value is 5k + 3k + 2k = 10k rupees. Setting 10k = 210 gives k = 21, so there are 126 coins of 50 paise. Check: 105 + 63 + 42 = 210.
hints: The ratio is of the number of coins, not their value.
Convert each group's value to rupees.
Total value is 10k rupees.

title: Hands meet between 4 and 5
statement: At what time between 4 o'clock and 5 o'clock are the hour and minute hands of a clock exactly together?
keySteps: At 4:00 the minute hand is 20 minute-spaces (120°) behind the hour hand.
The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute on the hour hand.
Time to catch up = 120 ÷ 5.5 = 240/11 = 21 9/11 minutes.
explanation: At 4:00 the hour hand is at 120° and the minute hand at 0°. The minute hand gains 6 − 0.5 = 5.5° every minute, so it closes the 120° gap in 120/5.5 = 240/11 = 21 9/11 minutes. Check: at that time the minute hand is at 6 × 240/11 ≈ 130.9° and the hour hand at 120 + 0.5 × 240/11 ≈ 130.9°.
hints: How far apart are the hands at exactly 4:00?
How fast does the minute hand gain on the hour hand?
Divide 120° by 5.5° per minute.

title: Family average after a child
statement:
When Vikram and Sita got married, their average age was 23 years. Five years later they have a child who is 1 year old.
What is the average age of the family of three now?
keySteps: At marriage their total age was 2 × 23 = 46.
Five years later the couple's total is 46 + 10 = 56.
Add the child: 56 + 1 = 57.
Average = 57 ÷ 3 = 19.
explanation: The couple's total age at marriage was 46, and after 5 years each is 5 years older, so 56. With the 1-year-old child the family total is 57, and the average is 57 ÷ 3 = 19. Check: 19 × 3 = 57.
hints: Turn the average into a total first.
Both husband and wife gain 5 years.
Divide the new total by 3 people.

title: Digits used for page numbers
statement:
A printer used a total of 2,993 digits to number all the pages of a book, starting from page 1.
How many pages does the book have?
keySteps: Pages 1–9 use 9 digits; pages 10–99 use 90 × 2 = 180 digits (189 so far).
Pages 100–999 use 900 × 3 = 2700 digits (2889 so far).
Remaining digits = 2993 − 2889 = 104, at 4 digits per page = 26 pages.
explanation: One-digit pages use 9 digits, two-digit pages 180, and three-digit pages 2700, totalling 2889 up to page 999. The remaining 104 digits are four-digit pages, 104 ÷ 4 = 26 of them, so the last page is 1025. Check: 9 + 180 + 2700 + 26 × 4 = 2993.
hints: Group the pages by how many digits their numbers have.
Find how many digits are used up to page 999.
The leftover digits all belong to four-digit page numbers.

title: Twice as old as he was
statement:
Arun is twice as old as Bharat was when Arun was as old as Bharat is now. The sum of their present ages is 63.
How old is Arun now?
keySteps: Let Arun = A and Bharat = B. Arun was B years old (A − B) years ago.
At that time Bharat was B − (A − B) = 2B − A.
Condition: A = 2(2B − A), so 3A = 4B.
With A + B = 63: B = 27 and A = 36.
explanation: Arun was Bharat's present age A − B years ago, when Bharat was 2B − A. So A = 2(2B − A), which gives 3A = 4B. Combined with A + B = 63, B = 27 and A = 36. Check: 9 years ago Arun was 27 and Bharat was 18, and 36 = 2 × 18.
hints: Ask how many years ago Arun was Bharat's present age.
That was (A − B) years ago — find Bharat's age then.
You should get 3A = 4B.

title: Slow clock on the fourth day
statement:
A clock is set right at 5:00 am on day 1. It loses 16 minutes every 24 hours (losing at a steady rate).
What is the true time when this clock shows 10:00 pm on day 4?
keySteps: From 5 am day 1 to 10 pm day 4 the clock shows 3 days + 17 hours = 89 hours.
In 24 real hours the clock shows 23 h 44 min = 356/15 hours.
Real hours = 89 × 24 ÷ (356/15) = 90 hours.
5:00 am day 1 + 90 hours = 11:00 pm day 4.
explanation: The clock shows 89 hours passing. It moves only 356/15 hours for every 24 real hours, so the real time is 89 × 24 × 15/356 = 90 hours. 90 hours after 5 am on day 1 is 11 pm on day 4. Check: in 90 real hours the clock loses 90/24 × 16 = 60 minutes, and 11 pm − 1 hour = 10 pm.
hints: First find how many hours the clock has shown since it was set.
A slow clock shows less time than really passes.
Scale 89 clock-hours by 24 / (23 h 44 min).

title: Same remainder divisor
statement: Find the largest number that divides 1305, 4665 and 6905 leaving the same remainder in each case.
keySteps: If they leave the same remainder, the divisor divides every difference.
The largest such number is 1120.
explanation: Numbers that leave equal remainders differ by multiples of the divisor, so the divisor must divide 3360, 2240 and 5600. Their HCF is 1120. Check: 1305 = 1120 + 185, 4665 = 4 × 1120 + 185, 6905 = 6 × 1120 + 185 — all leave 185.
hints: Equal remainders cancel when you subtract.
Work with the differences of the numbers.
Find the HCF of 3360, 2240 and 5600.

title: Two men replaced by two women
statement:
The average age of 8 men increases by 2 years when two of them, aged 21 and 23, are replaced by two women.
What is the average age of the two women?
keySteps: The group's total age rises by 8 × 2 = 16 years.
The two women together are 16 years more than the men they replaced: 21 + 23 + 16 = 60.
Average of the women = 60 ÷ 2 = 30.
explanation: An increase of 2 in the average of 8 people means the total grew by 16. The women replaced men totalling 44, so the women total 44 + 16 = 60, an average of 30. Check: replacing 44 with 60 adds 16 to the total, which is 2 per person over 8 people.
hints: Convert the change in average into a change in total.
Only the two replaced people change the total.
Women's total = men removed + 16.

title: Wrongly entered mark
statement:
In a class test, a student's mark was wrongly entered as 83 instead of 63. Because of this, the class average went up by half a mark.
How many students are in the class?
keySteps: The wrong entry adds 83 − 63 = 20 marks to the total.
This raises the average by 1/2, so 20 ÷ n = 1/2.
explanation: The total was inflated by 20 marks. Spread over n students, that raised the average by 20/n, which equals 1/2, so n = 40. Check: 20 extra marks over 40 students is 0.5 per student.
hints: How much was the total wrongly increased by?
Extra marks ÷ number of students = increase in average.

title: When 2027's calendar repeats
statement:
2027 is not a leap year and starts on a Friday.
In which year after 2027 can the 2027 calendar be used again exactly (same weekdays for every date)?
keySteps: A normal year moves the next year's start by 1 day; a leap year by 2.
We need a non-leap year starting on Friday.
Starts: 2028 Sat (leap), 2029 Mon, 2030 Tue, 2031 Wed, 2032 Thu (leap), 2033 Sat, 2034 Sun, 2035 Mon, 2036 Tue (leap), 2037 Thu, 2038 Fri.
2038 is not a leap year and starts on Friday, so it is the answer.
explanation: Each ordinary year shifts the starting weekday by 1 and each leap year by 2. We need the total shift to be a multiple of 7 and the target year to be non-leap. Adding odd days from 2027 to 2037 (8 ordinary + 3 leap) gives 8 + 6 = 14, a multiple of 7, and 2038 is non-leap. Check: no earlier year works — for example 2033 starts on Saturday.
hints: Track how many days the weekday of 1 January shifts each year.
Leap years shift by 2 days.
You need a non-leap year with total shift 0 mod 7.

title: Hands opposite in a day
statement: In one full day of 24 hours, how many times are the hour and minute hands of a clock exactly opposite each other (pointing in a straight line in opposite directions)?
keySteps: The minute hand gains a full lap on the hour hand 11 times in 12 hours.
In each lap the hands are opposite exactly once.
So they are opposite 11 times in 12 hours.
explanation: Every time the minute hand gains 360° on the hour hand, the gap passes through 180° once. That happens 11 times in 12 hours, so 22 times in 24 hours. Check: the hours 5–6 and 6–7 share the single opposite position at 6:00, which is why it is not 24.
hints: Opposite means the gap between the hands is 180°.
How many times does the minute hand lap the hour hand in 12 hours?
One opposite position per lap.

title: Remainder 3 and divisible by 9
statement: Find the smallest positive number that leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 5, 6 or 7, and is exactly divisible by 9.
keySteps: LCM(5, 6, 7) = 210, so the number is 210k + 3.
210 leaves remainder 3 by 9, so 210k + 3 has the same remainder as 3k + 3.
Need 3k + 3 divisible by 9, i.e. k + 1 divisible by 3; smallest k = 2.
explanation: Numbers with remainder 3 for 5, 6 and 7 are 210k + 3. Trying k = 0, 1, 2 gives 3, 213, 423; 3 and 213 are not divisible by 9 (digit sums 3 and 6) but 423 is (digit sum 9). Check: 423 = 9 × 47, and 423 − 3 = 420 is divisible by 5, 6 and 7.
hints: A common remainder means the number is LCM × k + 3.
Test 213, 423, ... with the digit-sum rule for 9.

title: Four-digit number divisible by 72
statement:
The four-digit number 4x7y (x and y are single digits) is divisible by 72.
What is the number?
keySteps: 72 = 8 × 9, so the number must be divisible by both 8 and 9.
Divisible by 9: 4 + x + 7 + y = 11 + x + y must be 18 or 27, so x + y = 7 or 16.
Divisible by 8: the last three digits x7y must be divisible by 8, so y is even.
Check candidates: only x = 1, y = 6 works (176 = 8 × 22, and 1 + 6 = 7).
The number is 4176.
explanation: For 9, x + y must be 7 or 16. For 8, x7y must be a multiple of 8. Pairs with x + y = 7 and y even: 770, 572, 374, 176 — only 176 is divisible by 8. With x + y = 16 and y even, the only pair is (8, 8), and 878 is not divisible by 8. So the number is 4176. Check: 4176 ÷ 72 = 58.
hints: Split 72 into two coprime factors.
Use the digit sum for 9 and the last three digits for 8.
x + y is 7 or 16; test which pair makes x7y divisible by 8.

title: Reversed-digit ages
statement:
Venkat's age is his son's age with the two digits reversed (both ages are two-digit numbers). In 7 years, Venkat will be exactly twice as old as his son.
How old is Venkat now?
keySteps: Let the son be 10a + b, so Venkat is 10b + a.
Condition: 10b + a + 7 = 2(10a + b + 7).
Simplify: 8b − 19a = 7.
Only a = 3, b = 8 fits single digits (64 − 57 = 7), so the son is 38 and Venkat is 83.
explanation: Writing the son as 10a + b and Venkat as 10b + a, the condition simplifies to 8b = 19a + 7. For digits, a = 3 gives 8b = 64, b = 8; no other a gives a whole digit b (a = 1 gives 26/8, a = 2 gives 45/8, a ≥ 4 makes b > 9). So the son is 38 and Venkat is 83. Check: in 7 years they are 45 and 90, and 90 = 2 × 45.
hints: Write both ages with digits a and b.
Form one equation from the condition in 7 years.

title: Fewest weights for a balance
statement:
A shopkeeper uses a two-pan balance and may place weights on both pans (weights can go on the same pan as the goods). He wants to weigh every whole number of kilograms from 1 kg to 40 kg.
What is the smallest number of weights he needs?
keySteps: With weights on both pans, each weight can be added, subtracted or unused: 3 choices.
n weights give at most (3^n − 1)/2 positive amounts; for n = 3 that is 13, fewer than 40.
For n = 4 that is 40, so 4 is the minimum if a set exists.
Weights 1, 3, 9 and 27 kg reach every value 1 to 40 (e.g. 2 = 3 − 1, 20 = 27 + 3 − 9 − 1).
explanation: Each weight can be on the opposite pan, on the goods' pan, or off the balance, so n weights produce at most (3^n − 1)/2 different positive loads. Three weights give at most 13, too few; four give up to 40. The powers of 3 — 1, 3, 9, 27 kg — achieve all of 1 to 40. Check: 40 = 1 + 3 + 9 + 27 and 14 = 27 − 9 − 3 − 1.
hints: Each weight has three possible positions.
Count how many different loads 3 weights could possibly give.
Try weights that are powers of 3.

title: Sharing Rs 1260 three ways
statement:
Rs 1,260 is divided among Anitha, Balu and Chandra. Anitha gets 2/3 of what Balu and Chandra get together. Balu gets 1/2 of what Anitha and Chandra get together.
How much does Chandra get, in rupees?
keySteps: A = (2/3)(B + C) means A is 2 parts and B + C is 3 parts, so A = 2/5 × 1260 = 504.
B = (1/2)(A + C) means B is 1 part of 3, so B = 1/3 × 1260 = 420.
explanation: If A is 2/3 of the others, then A : (B + C) = 2 : 3, so A gets 2/5 of 1260 = 504. Similarly B : (A + C) = 1 : 2, so B gets 1/3 of 1260 = 420. Chandra gets the rest, 336. Check: B + C = 756 and 2/3 of 756 = 504; A + C = 840 and half of 840 = 420.
hints: Turn 'A gets 2/3 of the other two' into a share of the total.
A : (B + C) = 2 : 3, so A gets 2/5 of the total.
Do the same for Balu, then subtract.

title: Two clocks drifting apart
statement:
Two clocks are set to the correct time at 12 noon on Monday. One gains 2 minutes every hour and the other loses 1 minute every hour.
After how many real hours will the two clocks next show exactly the same time?
keySteps: Every real hour the gap between the clocks grows by 2 + 1 = 3 minutes.
Clock faces show the same time again when the gap is 12 hours = 720 minutes.
explanation: The fast clock pulls ahead of the slow clock by 3 minutes per real hour. Their faces read the same again once the difference is a full 12 hours, which is 720 minutes, so after 720/3 = 240 hours (10 days). Check: by then the fast clock has gained 480 min (8 h) and the slow one lost 240 min (4 h); 8 h ahead and 4 h behind differ by 12 h, the same reading on a 12-hour face.
hints: Track the difference between the two clocks, not each clock alone.
How large must the difference be for the faces to look identical?
A 12-hour face repeats every 720 minutes.

title: Independence Day 1947 weekday
statement:
On which day of the week did 15 August 1947 fall?
(Use odd days: 1600 years have 0 odd days, every 100 years after that adds 5, an ordinary year adds 1 and a leap year adds 2.)
keySteps: 1600 years: 0 odd days; years 1601–1900 (300 years): 3 × 5 = 15, i.e. 1 odd day.
Years 1901–1946 (46 years) have 11 leap years and 35 ordinary: 22 + 35 = 57, i.e. 1 odd day.
1947 up to 15 August (not a leap year): 31+28+31+30+31+30+31+15 = 227 days, i.e. 3 odd days.
Total = 0 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 5 odd days, and 5 corresponds to Friday (0 = Sunday).
explanation: Count odd days through 15 August 1947: the first 1600 years give 0, the next 300 give 15 (1 odd day), 1901–1946 give 57 (1 odd day), and 1 January–15 August 1947 is 227 days (3 odd days). Total 5 odd days, and with 0 = Sunday, 5 = Friday. Check: 26 January 1950 was a Thursday; it is 895 days after 15 August 1947, which is 6 odd days, and Friday + 6 = Thursday.
hints: Split 1946 complete years into 1600 + 300 + 46.
Count leap years from 1901 to 1946 (1904, 1908, ..., 1944).
Add the days from 1 January to 15 August 1947 and reduce mod 7.
